materials.judgment: NVIDIA remains the main external accelerator system bottleneck because GB200 is a rack-scale system, but AMD MI300/MI35x and Google TPU are real workload-specific substitutes.

materials.cannot_infer: Cannot infer SKU revenue, share, shipment, ASP or margin from specs/benchmarks/cloud surfaces.
materials.counter_read: If AMD/TPU production deployments broaden or GB200 deployment slips, NVIDIA pricing and allocation power weakens.
materials.what_would_change_view: Production deployments, procurement mix and pricing evidence would change the weight.

materials.judgment: Dell has unusually visible AI server revenue demand, but the investment-quality question is margin conversion, not whether demand exists.
materials.business_mechanism: The right bridge is orders/backlog -> shipments -> ISG revenue -> gross/operating margin -> cash conversion. Current public rows prove the first half and leave AI server mix, GPU pass-through and attach economics unresolved.
materials.cannot_infer: Cannot call Dell AI server growth high-margin until AI server gross margin, GPU pass-through, attach rate and backlog conversion are disclosed.
materials.counter_read: Revenue tailwind may be low-margin GPU pass-through, with working-capital pressure or customer concentration.
materials.what_would_change_view: Improving ISG margin with backlog conversion and attach economics would strengthen Dell quality.

materials.judgment: AI read-through is strongest when split by mechanism: TSMC advanced node, ASML lithography/installed base, AMAT materials engineering and LRCX memory/HBM process intensity.
materials.business_mechanism: Peer group membership is not evidence. The product graph should map advanced-node/HBM/packaging demand into specific tool mechanisms and keep bookings/backlog/customer allocation as follow-up requirements.
materials.cannot_infer: Cannot infer AI-specific orders or customer allocation from broad revenue/margin alone.
materials.counter_read: Export controls, China exposure, memory/foundry cycle shifts, or missing bookings can break the read-through.
materials.what_would_change_view: Bookings/backlog by tool category, HBM/advanced packaging orders and customer concentration would change confidence.

materials.cannot_infer: Cannot infer customer concentration, deployment scale, or revenue per customer.

materials.what_would_change_view: Official customer deployments and GA cloud capacity would upgrade this lane.

supported_claims.judgment: Dell has unusually visible AI server revenue demand, but the investment-quality question is margin conversion, not whether demand exists.

supported_claims.what_would_change: Improving ISG margin with backlog conversion and attach economics would strengthen Dell quality.

supported_claims.judgment: AI read-through is strongest when split by mechanism: TSMC advanced node, ASML lithography/installed base, AMAT materials engineering and LRCX memory/HBM process intensity.

supported_claims.cannot_infer: Cannot infer AI-specific orders or customer allocation from broad revenue/margin alone.
supported_claims.counter_thesis: Export controls, China exposure, memory/foundry cycle shifts, or missing bookings can break the read-through.
supported_claims.what_would_change: Bookings/backlog by tool category, HBM/advanced packaging orders and customer concentration would change confidence.

supported_claims.judgment: Dell and Google provide official deployment surfaces that make GB200 adoption plausible, but public evidence still needs customer/order/config mix for investment-grade deployment quality.

supported_claims.cannot_infer: Cannot infer customer concentration, deployment scale, or revenue per customer.
supported_claims.counter_thesis: Preview-stage cloud availability or concentrated mega orders could limit the adoption signal.
supported_claims.what_would_change: Official customer deployments and GA cloud capacity would upgrade this lane.

supported_claims.judgment: The business chain is directionally positive, but recommendation quality is blocked by missing valuation, positioning, short/options, ETF flow and price-reaction data.
